messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A temporary fix used to expose a fault. the one part you expected to use turns out to be missing. Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i leave the faulty part where it is, then check the other side. i leave the fault in place, then leave the faulty one. i do not know whether the fault is a loose screw or a faulty sensor."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i tap the part that turned out to be it. i put the other half back in the box. the wrench taps once. i leave the part open, then turn the box over. the fault is still there, but the box is open."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I keep the old joint, but tap the old hinge with my thumb. I press a folded cloth over the missing hinge and test the hinge with a folded strip of paper. I leave the cloth on the old joint, but I tap the cloth twice and keep the paper. I leave the old hinge seated, but I keep counting the bend."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "i put the wrong part. i move the half-eaten board. the fault stays. i put the wrong nail in the gap. i wait. the fault stays. i put the wrong tool in the wrong place. the wrong tool. i put the nail in the wrong board."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i turn the faulty part over, then leave it on the table. i tap the nearest nail with a rusted bolt. “useful,” i say. i pocket the bolt’s edge. “one piece, not two.” i move the nail closer. “new thing.”"}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i put the old part back and mark the spot with a pencil. “i know the fault is there, but i still put the old part in the socket.” i leave the new one in the socket. sorry. i leave the old one in the drawer."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "the fault stays. the part breaks. i press the old strip with my thumb. the strip turns yellow. i put the new strip on, then the old one. the fault shifts. i put the old strip on the old one, then the new one. the fault stays. i remember the old strip tapping under the bench. i put the new one on the bench, then the old one. the fault shifts again. i put the old strip on the bench and forget the new one. the fault stays."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i photograph the faulty part and leave it behind. then i try the original solution: unplug it and leave the cover open. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the battery anyway."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i check the faulty part and put it in a small container. then i check the original log again and replace the missing one. i keep the original note and mark the original location. i trust the container’s log more than the original one."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i rub my palm and try the part I expected. i mark where it slipped, then put it back on the bench. if the fault shows, i leave the old fix behind and watch the fault move. i also test the new part, if it fails, i know where to look."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i hold the faulty part against my skin and trace the seam with my thumbnail. i leave the original part alone and mark the missing one with a pencil mark. i put the temporary fix in the sink and wait for the seam to heal on its own."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "\"Missing. I mark the wrong part. It stays. I check the watch. Likely.\" I take the faulty piece and place it beside the rest. I keep it tidy, but I know the sequence."}]
